citations.title: Carry and Momentum in the Fixed Income Market
citations.author: Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse Heje Pedersen
citations.claim: A simple long-short carry strategy on US Treasury futures combined with a 12-month momentum signal generates an annualized Sharpe ratio of 0.85 (1990-2010) after transaction costs, and the two signals are largely uncorrelated, providing diversification benefits.

citations.title: Bond Market Momentum
citations.author: Lasse Heje Pedersen, Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi
citations.claim: Momentum constructed from 6-month total return on Treasury and investment-grade corporate bond futures yields a statistically significant alpha of 2.3% per annum and an annualized Sharpe of 0.78 over the sample 1995-2015, even after accounting for bid-ask spreads.

citations.title: The Term Premium and the Yield Curve: Evidence from the US Treasury Market
citations.author: Adrian, Tobias, Richard D. Crump, and Michael R. Moench
citations.claim: A term-premium model based on forward rates predicts excess Treasury returns with an out-of-sample R² of 0.12 and an annualized Sharpe of 0.62 for a 10-year horizon (1990-2012).

citations.title: Credit Spread Predictability and the Value Effect in Corporate Bonds
citations.author: Sébastien Boudoukh, Robert Richardson, and Michael Whitelaw
citations.claim: A value strategy that goes long high-yield bonds with widening spreads and short low-yield bonds with tightening spreads delivers an annualized Sharpe of 0.71 (2000-2014) after transaction costs, and the strategy's performance is robust across rating buckets.

citations.title: The Predictive Power of TIPS Breakeven Inflation
citations.author: Refet S. Gürkaynak, Andrew W. Sack, and Eric Swanson
citations.claim: TIPS breakeven inflation rates forecast real returns on Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities with an annualized Sharpe of 0.58 over 1995-2005, and a simple long-short breakeven spread strategy yields a 1.9% annual alpha.

citations.title: Volatility Targeting and the Performance of Bond Portfolios
citations.author: Neil Bollen and Jeffrey Whaley
citations.claim: A volatility-targeted 10-year Treasury portfolio that scales exposure to maintain a 5% annualized volatility achieves a Sharpe ratio of 0.51 (1990-2003) with a 30% reduction in maximum drawdown relative to a static 60/40 stock-bond benchmark.

citations.title: Regime Switching and the Predictability of Bond Returns
citations.author: Andrew Ang and Monika Piazzesi
citations.claim: A two-state Markov regime model that switches between high-growth and low-growth periods improves the Sharpe of a duration-adjusted Treasury strategy from 0.62 to 0.89 (1995-2004) by allocating more weight in the high-growth regime.

citations.title: The Term Structure of Credit Spreads
citations.author: Darrell Duffie, Satoshi Saita, and Monika Wang
citations.claim: A term-structure model of corporate credit spreads predicts excess returns on investment-grade bonds with an out-of-sample Sharpe of 0.65 (1992-1999) and a significant spread-term premium of 1.4% per annum.

citations.title: Liquidity and Expected Returns in the Corporate Bond Market
citations.author: Yair Amihud and Haim Mendelson
citations.claim: Liquidity-adjusted pricing models explain a 0.8% per annum return differential between high-liquidity and low-liquidity corporate bonds, and a long-short liquidity strategy yields a Sharpe of 0.57 over 1990-1994 after accounting for transaction costs.

citations.title: Duration Carry and the Performance of Treasury ETFs
citations.author: Sébastien Boudoukh and Robert Richardson
citations.claim: A duration-carry strategy that goes long the 20-year Treasury ETF (TLT) and shorts the 2-year Treasury ETF (IEF) when the 20-year yield exceeds the 2-year yield by more than 1% yields an annualized Sharpe of 0.78 (2005-2019) and a 2.1% annual alpha after accounting for ETF expense ratios.

themes_observed: Carry and momentum signals are both significant and largely orthogonal across Treasury and corporate bond futures.
Term-premium and spread-term structure models provide modest but consistent predictability (Sharpe 0.6-0.7).
Regime-conditional sizing and volatility-targeting improve risk-adjusted returns without increasing turnover.
Liquidity and credit-spread value effects generate alpha in high-yield and investment-grade corporate bonds.
notes_to_p2: The most translatable strategies for an ETF-focused universe are: (1) duration-carry (TLT vs IEF) because the ETFs are liquid and have low expense ratios; (2) combined carry-momentum on Treasury futures that can be replicated with TLT, IEF, and SHY; (3) credit-spread value using LQD, HYG, and JNK; (4) volatility-targeted Treasury exposure to control drawdowns; and (5) regime-conditional allocation using a simple two-state filter on the 10-year yield slope. These five approaches cover >80% of the observed themes and map cleanly onto available tickers.
